sources.fact: Four directors backed +25bp, two favored holding, and one initially favored +50bp. The majority argued that headline/core inflation remained above 6%, expectations were unanchored, demand exceeded output and Niño/energy/oil/FX risks could reinforce inflation; it considered inflation-risk management supportive of a declining 2027 path. The two hold voters emphasized a highly restrictive real ex-post rate (about 6%), 275bp of hikes since end-2025, transmission lags, supply/indexation-driven persistence, and costs of further increases. The +50bp voter saw upside risks and argued delay could make later disinflation more costly. Minutes say future Niño effects, post-earthquake recovery and fiscal measures matter for subsequent decisions. This documents a split and conditional arguments, not a commitment to another hike or hold.
